crossrefs.text: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.
Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.
Better a little with righteousness than great gain with injustice.
Furthermore, I saw under the sun that in the place of judgment there is wickedness, and in the place of righteousness there is wickedness.
Do not be like Cain, who belonged to the evil one and murdered his brother. And why did Cain slay him? Because his own deeds were evil, while those of his brother were righteous.
Better is the little of the righteous than the abundance of many who are wicked.
Better a dry morsel in quietness than a house full of feasting with strife.

If you see the oppression of the poor and the denial of justice and righteousness in the province, do not be astonished at the matter; for one official is watched by a superior, and others higher still are over them.
As iron sharpens iron, so one man sharpens another.
The LordGod also said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make for him a suitable helper.”
But in fact, God has arranged the members of the body, every one of them, according to His design.
The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you.” Nor can the head say to the feet, “I do not need you.”
I cannot carry all these people by myself; it is too burdensome for me.
Then Jesus called the Twelve to Him and began to send them out two by two, giving them authority over unclean spirits.
Therefore encourage and build one another up, just as you are already doing.
Already the reaper draws his wages and gathers a crop for eternal life, so that the sower and the reaper may rejoice together.
So Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of the dungeon. After he had shaved and changed his clothes, he went in before Pharaoh.
He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the dump
to seat them with nobles, with the princes of His people.
He sets the lowly on high, so that mourners are lifted to safety.
Now, therefore, Pharaoh should look for a discerning and wise man and set him over the land of Egypt.
And Pharaoh declared to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but without your permission, no one in all the land of Egypt shall lift his hand or foot.”
And Jehoiakim rested with his fathers, and his son Jehoiachin reigned in his place.
Jehoiachin king of Judah, his mother, his servants, his commanders, and his officials all surrendered to the king of Babylon. So in the eighth year of his reign, the king of Babylon took him captive.
